debate_title: AI governance frameworks for advanced AI systems

conflicts.point: Whether the National Institute of Standards and Technology can enforce strict pre-market safety-gated deployment rules for frontier installations exceeding hundred-million-dollar compute thresholds while preserving permissionless access for small-scale open-weight researchers.

positions.stance: Argues that hard compute thresholds provide a bright-line rule that prevents administrative creep and protects open-source innovation while targeting unaligned frontier installations.
Maintains that statutory compute thresholds cannot prevent regulatory agencies from expanding administrative oversight downward through contractual liability chains.

verdicts.conflict: Whether the National Institute of Standards and Technology can enforce strict pre-market safety-gated deployment rules for frontier installations exceeding hundred-million-dollar compute thresholds while preserving permissionless access for small-scale open-weight researchers.
verdicts.rationale: The debate balances verifiable training costs against unprovable administrative creep. Safety advocates cite concrete financial thresholds above one hundred million dollars, whereas skeptics point to historical precedent where financial regulations expanded downward. Neither side offers definitive proof regarding whether peer-to-peer distribution channels can permanently evade institutional compliance mandates.
